note: ENGLISH_MAP.md probes. Written for the map; none copied from tests/battery. Story probes: each story is fed sentence by sentence (split after . ! ?), then each question asked. Question probes: one live door, in order; 'setup' turns are said first. gold: any listed string in the reply (battery.hit); '@ABSTAIN' = an abstention is the right outcome; '@DICT' = a dictionary definition is the right outcome; gold_all: every string must appear. pred/pred_door: R(IGHT) / W(RONG) / S(ILENT), predicted from the code BEFORE running.

stories.text: Nadia painted the fence. Later Omar washed the car.

qs.why: -ed form in the verb table; agent = nearest noun run on the left
agent run 'Later Omar' still contains omar; patient 'car'

stories.text: Kofi broke the vase. Then he swept the floor.
Lena found a coin. She made a wish.

qs.why: events3 main-verb rule: a name right before a closed verb form makes an event
'made' after a pronoun and 'make' are closed-class: no event, no question lemma

stories.text: Every morning Pablo feeds the chickens. His sister milks the cow.

qs.why: -s form after a noun is a verb (events6 A); agent run 'Every morning Pablo' contains pablo

stories.text: Sara lost her watches. Her brother watches the kids.

qs.why: after 'her' a third-person form is a noun (events6 A)
after a noun the same form is a verb; question lemma watch

stories.text: Paco didn't see the deer. His dog saw it.

qs.why: 'see' after 't' is closed-class (no event); 'saw it' finds no earlier patient -> see(dog, None) shares nothing with 'deer'
no event with Paco; polarity not represented

stories.text: Maya's dog chased the cat.

qs.why: agent run stops at 's: 'dog'; both roles filled, no adjunct to return

stories.text: A dog found a bone. The dog buried the bone.
The tall woman lifted the heavy box.

qs.q: What did the tall woman lift?

stories.text: The fire truck blocked the bus stop.

qs.q: What did the fire truck block?
qs.why: 'stop' is a base form, not finite -> noun

stories.text: The captain of the ship rang the bell.

qs.why: learned linker 'of' extends the run (events6 C)

qs.q: What did the captain of the ship ring?

stories.text: Sam, the old fisherman, caught a huge fish.

qs.why: the name is not linked to 'fisherman': no role shares 'sam'

stories.text: Lucas lost his keys. His mother found them under the sofa.

qs.why: 'found' is closed in the question; 'keys' is a verb form (key) -> the only lemma is 'key'

qs.q: Where did his mother find the keys?
qs.why: 'keys' is not content (verb form) -> patient not filled -> answers 'keys'

stories.text: Three boys climbed the hill. Each boy carried a flag.

qs.q: How many boys climbed the hill?
qs.why: no count role; both roles filled, no adjunct

stories.text: Ana bought 12 apples and 3 pears.

qs.q: How many apples did Ana buy?

stories.text: Mary Ann Evans wrote a long novel.

qs.q: What did Mary Ann Evans write?

stories.text: Captain Reyes steered the ship. Doctor Lim treated the sailors.

qs.why: title + name is one noun run

stories.text: Ivan walked to the fair. A man sold him a horse.

qs.why: 'man' is closed -> read as a pronoun -> last agent Ivan (honesty risk)

stories.text: A stranger knocked on the door. The stranger asked for water.

qs.why: 'water' closed so the question has no content; most recent 'ask' event

qs.q: What did the stranger ask for?
qs.why: 'water' closed -> no patient -> falls back to last patient 'door'

stories.text: Eva and Karl painted the barn.
The cat scratched the girl. The girl cried.
The baby slept in the car.

qs.why: PP object taken as patient (skips 'in the'); the answer is still the car

stories.text: Mia gave Leo a book.

qs.why: the recipient is stored as patient -> answers 'Leo'

stories.text: Nora gave a scarf to her sister.

qs.q: Who did Nora give the scarf to?

stories.text: Nina picked up the phone. Then she put down the cup.
Omar took a long walk by the river.
Hana was a nurse. Her husband was a pilot.

qs.why: be(Hana, nurse) is stored, but 'was' is closed so the question has no lemma
same; in the door the dictionary likely quotes a gloss instead

stories.text: There was a well behind the house. A frog lived in the well.

qs.why: 'There was' makes no event (no noun before 'was')
'well' closed -> no content -> most recent 'live' agent

stories.text: Sana wanted to learn the violin.

qs.q: What did Sana want to learn?
qs.why: infinitive event learn(Sana, violin) is most recent among equal scores

stories.text: Mira told Tomas to close the gate.

qs.q: Who did Mira tell to close the gate?

qs.why: infinitive takes the clause's first agent (Mira): object control not modelled

stories.text: Ella made her brother wash the dishes.

qs.why: bare 'wash' is read as a noun inside 'brother wash'; no wash event

qs.q: Who made her brother wash the dishes?
qs.why: 'made' closed in the question; 'dishes' -> lemma dish

stories.text: Lina heard the dog bark.

qs.why: no bark event (bare form read as a noun)

stories.text: The window was broken by a stone.

qs.why: stored reversed (agent=window, patient=stone); an active question reverses back
passive question returns the stored patient 'stone' (honesty risk)

stories.text: The letters were burned in the stove.

qs.why: same slip gives the right answer by accident

stories.text: Pedro got bitten by a snake.

qs.why: 'got' is not a learned auxiliary -> no 'bite' event

stories.text: Grandpa planted the oak tree in 1950.

qs.q: When was the oak tree planted?
qs.why: events5 E: passive question with patient named -> adjuncts

qs.q: By whom was the oak tree planted?

stories.text: Lara was reading a letter. Her cat was sleeping on the bed.
Tom has fixed the roof.

qs.why: 'has' + participle in the QUESTION reads as passive (events5 E); patient named, no adjunct -> nothing

stories.text: Tomorrow Ada will visit her aunt.

qs.why: an infinitive event in the first sentence takes no agent (none before it)

stories.text: Ada cooked dinner. Later she will wash the plates.

qs.why: future stored as a plain event; answers 'plates'

stories.text: Inspector Ross searched the house. The thief may have taken the ring.

qs.why: 'thief' 2 closed symbols away; 'have' read as a pronoun -> last agent Inspector Ross (honesty risk)

stories.text: If Leo wins, his father will buy a boat.

qs.why: infinitive takes the sentence's first agent Leo

qs.q: Did his father buy a boat?

stories.text: If Ben had studied, he would have passed the exam.

qs.why: pass(Ben, exam) stored as fact (honesty risk)

stories.text: Ivy plays the piano every evening.

qs.why: patient run 'piano every evening' contains piano

stories.text: Rosa cooked dinner. She didn't eat the soup.

qs.why: 't' is a learned marker -> eat(Rosa, soup) stored as fact (honesty risk)

stories.text: Kai never visited Lima.

qs.why: 'never' is not closed -> agent run 'Kai never'; the reply happens to say 'never'

stories.text: No guest drank the wine.
Nobody opened the gift.
Two dogs ran into the yard. The black dog dug a hole.

qs.why: agent 'black dog' and patient both filled; no adjunct

stories.text: Bea hid the key under the mat.

qs.q: Where did Bea hide the key?

stories.text: On Sunday the family visited the zoo.

qs.q: When did the family visit the zoo?
qs.why: 'family' closed -> agent None; fronted time phrase not an adjunct

stories.text: Tim stayed home because he was sick.

qs.why: adjunct scan picks up 'he was sick'

stories.text: The road was closed, so Dan took the bus.

qs.q: Why did Dan take the bus?
qs.why: 'take' closed in the question -> no lemma

stories.text: Rita opened the jar with a knife.

qs.q: How did Rita open the jar?

stories.text: Leo won the race easily.

qs.q: How did Leo win the race?
qs.why: 'easily' joins the patient run; no adjunct left

stories.text: Ines washed the apples and peeled the pears.

qs.why: previous patient is not the next doer (events rule) -> shared agent

stories.text: Ali fed the goats, and his wife milked the cows.
When the bell rang, the children ran outside.
